title: Copilot Studio: cost controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center
summary: The roadmap facts, opt-in behaviour, billing rules and documented control references are supported. Minor checklist corrections remain: role-assignment and consumption-monitoring checks have no corresponding controls-table rows.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to expand Copilot Studio cost management into the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: We’re expanding cost management for Microsoft Copilot Studio into the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The roadmap retains Copilot Studio cost management capabilities in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: while retaining Copilot Studio cost management capabilities in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies for supported environments and agents are the first planned scopes.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies for environments and agents are the first planned scopes

claims.claim: Broader user and group policy support is planned for a later phase.
claims.quote: with broader user and group policy support planned for a later phase.

claims.where: What's changing, first paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap plans cost data in cost management and the agent registry for Microsoft-platform services and agents, including Cowork and Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: this update will introduce cost data into cost management and agent registry for AI services and agents built on Microsoft platforms (e.g., Cowork, Microsoft Copilot Studio agents).

claims.quote: "targetDate": "October CY2026"; the supplied verification run date is 2026-11-17.

claims.where: What's changing, final paragraph; Scope: Rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a tenant-complete rollout date or whether any particular tenant already has the experience.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio cost management generally available tenant; opened Manage Copilot Studio costs, the usage-based billing overview and setup pages. They document configuration, not a tenant-complete rollout date or an individual tenant's availability.

claims.where: What's changing, final paragraph; Scope: Rollout
claims.claim: Learn already describes policy creation despite the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, create a resource-based spending policy for the agent, resource, or environment you want to manage.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationales: risk, impact
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in: existing configuration continues unless an administrator creates a resource-based policy covering the scope.
claims.quote: To opt in, create a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy. Until then, your existing Power Platform admin center configuration remains in effect.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; controls[1].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A covering Microsoft 365 resource-based policy replaces the covered resources' Power Platform capacity allocations.
claims.quote: For resources covered by the spending policy, Copilot Credit management moves to the Microsoft 365 admin center, replacing their Power Platform admin center capacity allocations and linked billing plans.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; controls[3].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Linked Power Platform billing plans no longer apply while the environment is covered by a Microsoft 365 resource-based policy.
claims.quote: Existing Power Platform capacity allocations and linked billing plans don't apply while spending for that environment is managed by a resource-based spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: No separate migration step is required.
claims.quote: No separate migration step is required.

claims.where: What's changing, second paragraph; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Specific resource policies cover individually selected agents.
claims.quote: | **Specific resource** | Individual agents that you select. | Manage spending for a particular agent. |

claims.claim: Resource collection policies cover all supported usage in selected environments, including deployed apps and workflows.
claims.quote: | **Resource collection** | All supported usage in the environments that you select, including apps and workflows deployed in those environments.

claims.claim: Apps and workflows cannot be selected individually and must be covered through their environment.
claims.quote: Apps and workflows don't currently appear in the agent selector, so you can't select an individual app or workflow. To cover them, create a policy for the environment where they're deployed.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Resource-based policies allow a monthly spending limit or No limit.
claims.quote: Choose No limit or set a monthly spending limit for the policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An optional per-agent spending limit can be set within the policy.
claims.quote: You can also set a per-agent limit so that no single agent covered by the policy uses more than the amount you specify.

claims.claim: Policy setup includes alert thresholds and recipients.
claims.quote: Configure alert thresholds and recipients as needed.

claims.claim: Policy setup uses a default billing method or an available billing-method override.
claims.quote: Use the default billing method or choose an available billing-method override. Review the settings, then create the policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Removing an environment from a spending policy automatically resumes its applicable Power Platform policy.
claims.quote: If you remove an environment from a spending policy or delete the resource-based spending policy, the applicable Power Platform admin center policy resumes for that environment automatically.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Deleting the covering resource-based policy automatically resumes the applicable Power Platform policy.
claims.quote: The same fallback applies when you delete the Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy that covered it; no additional Power Platform setup is required.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says to allow up to 12 minutes after linking an environment for the policy to apply.
claims.quote: After you link an environment to a Microsoft 365 spending policy, allow up to 12 minutes for the new policy to apply.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Selecting All environments replaces existing Power Platform spending controls for every environment.
claims.quote: Selecting **All environments** applies the resource-based spending policy to every environment and replaces their existing Power Platform admin center spending controls.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn advises starting with Specific environments for a gradual transition.
claims.quote: Start with **Specific environments** to gradually transition spending management to the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: What's changing, final paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited agent-registry integration page lists no cost field in its visible metadata.
claims.quote: Searched: agent registry cost metadata. Opened Agent registry integration for Copilot Studio, including Visible metadata and Admin experience; its metadata lists contain no cost field. Search excerpts from the registry overview also supplied no cost field.

claims.claim: The Cost Management dashboard also serves other usage-based Copilot services and supports finance and licensing readers.
claims.quote: This separation enables finance, operations, licensing, and governance stakeholders to review consumption information with read-only access.

claims.claim: Management in the new experience requires Microsoft 365 roles rather than inheriting Power Platform administrative roles.
claims.quote: Assign roles before creating the first policy. The recommendations are role assignments to consider; an existing Power Platform role does not itself become a Microsoft 365 role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The documented change concerns spending controls, with no new content access or agent-action capability documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio cost management data access; usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-studio-costs data access. Read the feature, setup and overview pages; these describe spending, billing and consumption reporting, not new content permissions or agent actions.

claims.claim: Consumption views break down usage by policy, user, group, agent, service and funding source.
claims.quote: Review consumption by spending policy, user, group, agent, service, and funding source.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Supported reader roles, including AI Reader and Global Reader, can view consumption dashboards and reports without configuration permissions.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports. These roles provide read-only access to consumption information

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Global administrator can set billing methods.
claims.quote: Global administrator and Billing administrator roles can add, select, and change billing methods, and set billing methods in policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Billing administrator can set billing methods.
claims.quote: You must be a Global administrator or Billing administrator to override or set the billing method.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: AI administrator can edit spending policies, limits and alerts.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods.

claims.claim: License administrator can edit spending policies, limits and alerts according to the setup page.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The setup page explicitly says AI administrator cannot create spending policies.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: The setup page explicitly says License administrator cannot create spending policies.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: An existing Power Platform role does not itself grant Microsoft 365 policy rights.
claims.quote: an existing Power Platform role does not itself become a Microsoft 365 role.

claims.where: Scope: Roles; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature page recommends AI Administrator for Power Platform or Dynamics 365 Administrators managing spending policies.
claims.quote: | Power Platform Administrator or Dynamics 365 Administrator | AI Administrator | Manage spending policies. |

claims.claim: The feature page recommends AI Reader for Environment Administrators viewing consumption.
claims.quote: | Environment Administrator | AI Reader | View consumption when needed. |

claims.claim: The setup procedure lists Global administrator or Billing administrator for initial policy creation.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center with one of the following administrator roles:
- Global administrator
- Billing administrator

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; controls[2].note; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not specify the covered agent's precise runtime behaviour at a resource-based policy limit or confirm that Power Platform's hard stop still applies.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio resource-based limit reached; resource based spending policy limit reached agent blocked stops. Opened the feature and managing-spending-policies pages. The former specifies limits and no identity-policy fallback, not the precise runtime response.

claims.claim: Power Platform documents an agent-level hard-stop guardrail that turns the agent off at its limit.
claims.quote: After you set limits, you can configure two key guardrails: ... Hard stop: The agent is automatically turned off once it hits the defined limit.

claims.claim: Power Platform documents administrator notifications as an agent approaches its configured limit.
claims.quote: Notifications: Admins, both at the environment and tenant level, receive alerts when an agent's usage approaches the defined limit.

claims.claim: Power Platform agent limits are not applied instantly.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit, so set limits and notification thresholds with some margin.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 controls take precedence over Power Platform controls for covered environment or agent usage.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Resource-based policies exclude AI Builder features and their credits, and Learn says not to move AI Builder-using resources into these policies.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume. ... Don't move resources, agents, workflows or environments that use AI Builder to these policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: AI Builder powers prompts used as tools, in topics and as nodes in agent flows.
claims.quote: AI Builder powers prompts used as tools, in topics, and as nodes in agent flows.

claims.claim: A resource-based policy takes precedence over an identity-based policy.
claims.quote: Within the Microsoft 365 admin center, a policy for the agent or its environment takes precedence over a policy for the person using the agent.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Where resource-based policies overlap, the policy with the higher applicable per-agent limit applies.
claims.quote: If you have a resource-based All-environments policy and a Specific resource HR agent policy, the policy with the higher per-agent limit applies.

claims.claim: Overlapping policy limits are not added together.
claims.quote: Spending limits from overlapping policies aren't combined.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Power Platform's Manage capacity experience indicates when an environment's credits are managed by a Microsoft 365 resource-based policy.
claims.quote: the Manage capacity experience indicates when Copilot Credits for an environment are managed by a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Power Platform's Manage agent experience displays a message when a policy covers an agent.
claims.quote: The Manage agent experience also displays a message when an agent is covered by a policy.

claims.claim: The feature page's Before you begin section lists administrative roles and names no licence or control price.
claims.quote: Before creating a resource-based spending policy for Copilot Studio agents, ensure that you have the necessary roles in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate licence or charge for the cost control itself is stated in the documentation at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio cost controls Microsoft 365 admin center license additional charge rollout availability; Copilot Studio cost management separate license. Read the feature prerequisites, setup and billing overview; no separate control licence or charge is stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The governed usage has a consumption licensing model and variable cost measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Microsoft's usage-based billing model charges customers based on actual usage, measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The policy's selected Azure subscription is billed for Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are billed to the subscription that you select in the billing method.

claims.claim: When credits for the selected subscription run out, usage continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.
claims.quote: When credits run out for that subscription, usage automatically continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Copilot Credit Pre-purchase Plan (P3) is layered on top of pay-as-you-go rather than being a separate billing option.
claims.quote: Copilot Credit Pre‑Purchase Plan (P3) and pay‑as‑you-go aren't separate billing options. P3 is layered on top of pay‑as‑you-go.

claims.claim: P3 can be purchased from Cost Management > Configuration or through the Azure portal.
claims.quote: You can purchase a Copilot Credit Pre‑Purchase Plan (P3) from the Microsoft 365 admin center by selecting Buy Pre-purchase Credits on the Cost Management > Configuration page. You can also complete this step through the Azure portal.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: When both prepaid capacity packs and a P3 subscription are selected, the billing order is capacity packs, P3, then pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: If you select both Prepaid Capacity packs and an Azure subscription with Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3), billing is applied in the following order ... Prepaid Capacity packs ... Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3) ... Pay-as-you-go billing

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity pack credits can support services managed in either admin center.
claims.quote: Prepaid Capacity pack credits can support services managed in either admin center.

claims.claim: Credits allocated to Power Platform environments reduce credits available to other services in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Credits allocated to environments in the Power Platform admin center reduce the credits available for other services in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: An existing identity-based policy cannot be converted into a resource-based policy; a new resource-based policy must be created.
claims.quote: You can't convert an existing identity-based policy into a resource-based policy. To manage a resource or environment when you have only an identity-based policy, create a new resource-based policy.

claims.claim: The Graph Cost Management API overview documents spending-policy scopes for all users and selected groups.
claims.quote: Scope a policy to every user in the tenant (allUsersSpendingPolicy) or to selected groups (selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy).

claims.claim: The documented Graph API is beta, subject to change and unsupported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: controls[0].api; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No documented Graph call for resource-based environment or agent spending policies was found.
claims.quote: Searched: graph beta resource based spending policy environments agents cost management API. Read the Graph Cost Management API overview, its scope types and API list, plus the resource-policy feature page; only all-user and selected-group policy types are documented.

claims.claim: No Copilot Studio-specific monthly per-agent limit API is documented in the references checked.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio monthly per agent consumption limit API Dataverse bot pac licensing threshold; Copilot Studio monthly limit API threshold. Read pac licensing, resource-threshold REST and govern-credit-consumption; generic thresholds lack a Copilot Studio monthly-agent mapping.

claims.claim: Power Platform documents generic environment-resource threshold automation in pac licensing.
claims.quote: pac licensing upsert-resource-threshold ... (Preview) Create or update the resource threshold for an environment resource.

claims.claim: The cited pac licensing commands are marked Preview.
claims.quote:
pac licensing
(Preview) Manage licensing, entitlements, capacity, billing policies, and allocations.

claims.claim: Environment admin, Power Platform admin, Global admin and Dynamics 365 admin can create Power Platform billing policies, subject to Azure permissions.
claims.quote: | Environment admin | Yes | ... | Power Platform admin | Yes | ... | Global admin | Yes | ... | Dynamics 365 admin | Yes |

claims.claim: Environment admins can edit only billing policies they created and link only their own policies to environments they administer.
claims.quote: | Environment admin | Yes | Yes, for billing policies the admin created. | Yes, for billing policies the admin created and for environments in which they're admins. |

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go setup requires permission to create resources and register resource providers in the Azure subscription, or assistance from someone with those permissions.
claims.quote: You need to have permissions to create new resources and register resource providers in the subscription—or have the ability to work with another user who has these permissions.

claims.claim: Resource-based policy creation is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management.
Select Configuration, and then select Add spending policy.

claims.claim: Capacity allocation is reached through Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane, select Licensing. ... In the Licensing pane, under Products, select Copilot Studio. ... Select the Summary tab. ... Under the Copilot Studio heading, select Manage Copilot Credits or Manage sessions.

claims.claim: pac licensing update-allocations-by-environment updates environment allocations and enforcement rules.
claims.quote:
pac licensing update-allocations-by-environment
(Preview) Update currency allocations and enforcement rules for an environment.

claims.claim: Monthly agent consumption limits are reached through Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Agents.
claims.quote:
On the navigation pane, select Licensing.
In the Licensing pane, under Products, select Copilot Studio.
On the Summary tab, select Manage Agents.

claims.claim: Azure-backed billing-plan creation is at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Pay-as-you-go plans > New billing plan > Azure subscription.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Licensing. ... In the Licensing pane, select Pay-as-you-go plans. ... Select New billing plan. ... Select Azure subscription.

claims.claim: pac licensing create-billing-policy creates a billing policy, and add-billing-policy-environment links it using --billing-policy-id and JSON-array --environment-ids.
claims.quote: pac licensing create-billing-policy ... Creates the billing policy at tenant level. ... pac licensing add-billing-policy-environment ... Link billing policy ID with environments. ... --billing-policy-id ... --environment-ids ... Provide the value as a JSON array.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist's role-separation and role-assignment checks are represented by a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Separate policy creators, editors and consumption readers' and 'Agree who holds Global administrator or Billing administrator'. The four controls rows cover spending policies, capacity allocation, agent limits and billing plans, not role assignment.
claims.fix: Move the Before rollout advice about separating creators, editors and readers, and agreeing who holds Global administrator or Billing administrator, to Scope: Roles; the checklist has no corresponding role-assignment control row.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist's consumption-monitoring check is represented by a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Review consumption by environment and agent in Cost Management and compare it with the limits set.' The controls table has no consumption-monitoring row.
claims.fix: Move 'Review consumption by environment and agent in Cost Management and compare it with the limits set' from the After rollout checklist to the explanatory Governance controls prose; the checklist has no corresponding monitoring control row.
